subject: Walmart third-quarter earnings
title: Walmart earnings: Did Walmart beat estimates? Yes, and it raised its outlook
answer: Yes. On Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, Walmart reported third-quarter sales of $188.8 billion, up 5.2%, and adjusted earnings of 65 cents a share, both slightly above Wall Street forecasts. It raised its full-year outlook for the third time this year, though the new range came in a bit below what analysts expected.
in_the_news: Walmart serves more than 150 million shoppers a week, so its numbers are read as a gauge of U.S. consumers going into Thanksgiving and the holiday season. The report came days after government data showed retail sales grew just 0.2% in October.
body:
In the quarter that ended Oct. 31, comparable sales at Walmart U.S. rose 2.9%, better than 2.6% in the prior quarter, the weakest in six years, but slower than 4.5% a year earlier, AP reported. Groceries and general merchandise such as furniture and toys led the gain. Online sales grew 17% worldwide and 23% in the U.S., and more than 80% of U.S. online orders were filled from stores. Net income fell to $4.94 billion, or 62 cents a share, from $6.14 billion, or 77 cents, a year before. "We delivered strong results, growing our core business and gaining market share," CEO John Furner said.

Walmart now expects full-year sales growth of 4.9% to 5.2%, up from 4% to 5%, and adjusted earnings of $2.84 to $2.89 a share, up from $2.80 to $2.87. Analysts had expected $2.89 and about $752.7 billion in sales, above Walmart's implied range of roughly $748 billion to $750 billion. Shares rose nearly 1% before the opening bell. The company again said a federal price cap on some high-cost Medicare drugs, which its pharmacies must honor, held back its comparable sales.

The report in plain words: "Comparable sales" compare stores and websites that were open in both periods, so they show whether existing business grew rather than just new store openings. "Adjusted" earnings strip out one-time items, which is why Walmart reports 65 cents adjusted but 62 cents on a standard accounting basis; analysts' forecasts are usually for the adjusted figure. "Guidance" is the company's own forecast for the full year, and raising it means management now expects a better year than it did three months ago.

For shoppers, the takeaway is that Walmart is leaning on its low-price pitch and is winning business from households earning over $100,000 a year. It now sells a combined Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus annual bundle for $120, which it says saves nearly $100 versus buying both memberships separately. The next report will cover the holiday quarter, which ends Jan. 31, 2027, and closes Walmart's fiscal year.

faq.q: How much did Walmart earn per share in the third quarter?
faq.a: Adjusted earnings were 65 cents a share, against the 64 cents analysts expected. On a standard accounting basis, Walmart earned 62 cents a share.

faq.q: Did Walmart stock go up after earnings?
faq.a: Slightly. Shares rose by less than 1% in trading before the market opened on Nov. 19, as the raised outlook was a bit more cautious than analysts had hoped.

faq.q: Why are Walmart's results watched so closely?
faq.a: It is the largest U.S. retailer, with more than 150 million weekly customers, so its sales and forecast offer an early read on how Americans are spending ahead of the holidays.
